findings.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` required by ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8.x's `include_#{attr}?` override convention (all 10 sibling `include_*` methods in this same file use `?`), so this override is never picked up by `define_include_method` and `website_name` ends up unconditionally serialized (present with `null` when `website` is blank) rather than conditionally omitted as the code's naming/comment intent and the testing persona's assumption suggest — meaning the actual JSON contract shipped is "key always present," and a later typo-fix adding the `?` would silently flip the response shape to "key sometimes absent," a breaking change for any consumer that came to rely on the buggy-but-shipped always-present behavior

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137 — website_name` is not a simple hostname despite its name: when the website's domain matches or is a parent/sibling of the forum's own domain, the value becomes `host + path` (e.g. "example.com/user") instead of just the host, an undocumented value-shape variance that third-party clients treating "*_name" fields as short bare-hostname display strings could mishandle

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:59 — Checked and found benign: the JSDoc `@property` rename from `websiteName` to `profileBackground` is a pre-existing doc-typo fix on an unrelated CSS-background computed property (unchanged function body building a `background-image` style string) — coincidental naming collision with the new `website_name` API field, not a sign of confusion or an actual contract change

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Hostname comparisons in `website_name` (`website_host == discourse_host` at line 141, and the suffix comparisons at lines 146 and 149) are case-sensitive because `URI(...).host` is returned as-is (verified `URI("HTTP://WWW.EXAMPLE.COM").host` => "WWW.EXAMPLE.COM"), so a website entered with uppercase host that is otherwise identical to `Discourse.current_hostname` fails to match and the link renders as the bare (wrongly-cased) host instead of host+path, even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — A trailing dot on the website or discourse host (e.g. "example.com.") adds an extra empty label via `split('.')`, so the direct equality check and the length-gated subdomain checks (lines 144/146) fail to recognize two otherwise-identical hosts as the same domain

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:69 — {{model.website_name}}` is rendered with standard double-stash Handlebars interpolation (the codebase uses `{{{...}}}` elsewhere, e.g. line 84 for `bio_cooked`, when raw/unescaped HTML is intended), so Ember auto-escapes the server-computed host/path string and it cannot break out of the `<a>` text node or inject markup, even though the value now includes the attacker-controlled URI `.path` component

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:67 — No test covers `website_name` when website is blank/nil for a normal (non-TL0) user: `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` so the key is correctly omitted in that case, but this is never asserted, and the getter itself is never exercised with an empty string to confirm it doesn't raise before `include_website_name?` short-circuits.

spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — No test for case sensitivity (e.g. `Example.COM` vs `example.com`) or for trailing dot / port-number variations in either the website or the instance hostname, even though domain names are case-insensitive by spec while the implementation does plain string `==`/`ends_with?` comparisons that would fail on mixed case.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` required by ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8.x's `include_#{attr}?` override convention (all 10 sibling `include_*` methods in this same file use `?`), so this override is never picked up by `define_include_method` and `website_name` ends up unconditionally serialized (present with `null` when `website` is blank) rather than conditionally omitted as the code's naming/comment intent and the testing persona's assumption suggest — meaning the actual JSON contract shipped is "key always present," and a later typo-fix adding the `?` would silently flip the response shape to "key sometimes absent," a breaking change for any consumer that came to rely on the buggy-but-shipped always-present behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`) while intending conditional inclusion (`website.present?`). If the serializer framework expects the `include_<attr>?` predicate form (as the finding states), this method will not be invoked and `website_name` (added to `untrusted_attributes`) will be serialized unconditionally, potentially as `null` when `website` is blank—contrary to the apparent intent of `include_website_name`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137 — website_name` is not a simple hostname despite its name: when the website's domain matches or is a parent/sibling of the forum's own domain, the value becomes `host + path` (e.g. "example.com/user") instead of just the host, an undocumented value-shape variance that third-party clients treating "*_name" fields as short bare-hostname display strings could mishandle

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` in `UserSerializer#website_name` and it sometimes returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` (e.g. when `website_host == discourse_host` or when the forum is a subdomain of the website domain), not just the bare host. This is explicitly asserted by the new specs (e.g. expecting `example.com/user`), so it’s intentional behavior, but the field name `website_name` can reasonably be interpreted by consumers as a short hostname-only display string, making the shape variance a legitimate API/naming/compatibility concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6:59 — Checked and found benign: the JSDoc `@property` rename from `websiteName` to `profileBackground` is a pre-existing doc-typo fix on an unrelated CSS-background computed property (unchanged function body building a `background-image` style string) — coincidental naming collision with the new `website_name` API field, not a sign of confusion or an actual contract change

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes the JSDoc tag above the existing `profileBackground` computed property from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground` (function body unchanged). This is a straightforward documentation typo fix and not evidence of a contract/behavior change or confusion with the new `website_name` field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Hostname comparisons in `website_name` (`website_host == discourse_host` at line 141, and the suffix comparisons at lines 146 and 149) are case-sensitive because `URI(...).host` is returned as-is (verified `URI("HTTP://WWW.EXAMPLE.COM").host` => "WWW.EXAMPLE.COM"), so a website entered with uppercase host that is otherwise identical to `Discourse.current_hostname` fails to match and the link renders as the bare (wrongly-cased) host instead of host+path, even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` is compared directly against `Discourse.current_hostname` (`==` and `ends_with?`/split logic) without any case normalization. Since these string comparisons are case-sensitive, an uppercase/lowercase mismatch in the parsed host vs `current_hostname` would cause the “same host” / “parent host” branches to be skipped and fall back to returning just `website_host` (or other incorrect branch output), even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — A trailing dot on the website or discourse host (e.g. "example.com.") adds an extra empty label via `split('.')`, so the direct equality check and the length-gated subdomain checks (lines 144/146) fail to recognize two otherwise-identical hosts as the same domain

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic compares hosts via direct string equality (`website_host == discourse_host`) and uses `split('.')` length/content checks (e.g., `website_host.split('.').length ...`). If either `URI(website).host` or `Discourse.current_hostname` contains a trailing dot (e.g., `example.com.`), equality will fail and `split('.')` will include an extra empty label, changing lengths and subdomain comparisons, so two otherwise-identical domains may be treated as different and produce an incorrect `website_name`. This edge case is not normalized/handled in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:69 — {{model.website_name}}` is rendered with standard double-stash Handlebars interpolation (the codebase uses `{{{...}}}` elsewhere, e.g. line 84 for `bio_cooked`, when raw/unescaped HTML is intended), so Ember auto-escapes the server-computed host/path string and it cannot break out of the `<a>` text node or inject markup, even though the value now includes the attacker-controlled URI `.path` component

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `{{model.website_name}}` is interpolated with normal Handlebars mustaches in `user.hbs`, which in Ember/Handlebars is HTML-escaped by default, so the described XSS risk (breaking out of the `<a>` text node via the attacker-controlled `.path`) is not evidenced by the diff. The finding is effectively asserting safety rather than identifying a defect or actionable review issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:67 — No test covers `website_name` when website is blank/nil for a normal (non-TL0) user: `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` so the key is correctly omitted in that case, but this is never asserted, and the getter itself is never exercised with an empty string to confirm it doesn't raise before `include_website_name?` short-circuits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `website_name` attribute with nontrivial logic in `UserSerializer` plus `include_website_name` (which only includes the key when `website.present?`). The added specs cover several hostname/path scenarios when `website` is set, but there is no assertion for the blank/nil website case to confirm the key is omitted and that `website_name` remains safe on empty input (even though the implementation uses `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76 — No test for case sensitivity (e.g. `Example.COM` vs `example.com`) or for trailing dot / port-number variations in either the website or the instance hostname, even though domain names are case-insensitive by spec while the implementation does plain string `==`/`ends_with?` comparisons that would fail on mixed case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial hostname comparison logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` using plain string comparisons (`website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, and `split('.')`-based checks). The accompanying spec exercises only lowercase, no-port, no-trailing-dot cases (e.g. `example.com`, `forums.example.com`) and does not cover mixed-case hostnames or other hostname-normalization variants. Given the implementation depends on exact string equality/suffix matching, additional tests for normalization edge cases would be a reasonable, diff-grounded review request, even if it may not be a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.
